title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): S is a base scheme and M is a rank-4 Azumaya (quaternion) algebra over O_S. The groups are G = M^* (a form of GL_2), SG (the reduced-norm-1 subgroup, a form of SL_2) and PG (a form of PGL_2). P is the associated Brauer–Severi conic, a P^1-bundle over S. On the previous page Grothendieck sets up the following. A 'regular unipotent section' is e = 1+N with N regular nilpotent, meaning N^2 = 0 and N ≠ 0 on every fibre (Steinberg's terminology). Two such sections are identified when they differ by e ↦ e^λ = 1+λN with λ ∈ Γ(G_m). The equivalence classes correspond to Borel additive subgroups, i.e. unipotent radicals of Borel subgroups, hence to Borels, hence to sections x_∞ of P. Removing x_∞ makes P \ {x_∞} = E an affine line bundle.

This page:
(6) The section x_∞ is equivalently given by a one-parameter Borel additive subgroup L ⊂ SG ⊂ G, the unipotent radical of the Borel fixing x_∞. Its image under SG → PG is again such a subgroup of PG, since the centre μ_2 meets L trivially.
(7) Locally L is generated by a regular unipotent section e = 1+N.
(8) Through it L is the one-parameter group λ ↦ e^λ = 1+λN. Since N^2 = 0, this is literally exp(λN) = (1+N)^λ.
However e and N are not intrinsic to L: they are defined only up to N ↦ μN with μ a unit. Grothendieck observes that L nevertheless carries a canonical structure of rank-1 vector bundle, compatible with conjugation by G. It is obtained by transporting the vector-space structure of G_a along the isomorphism e: G_a → L, λ ↦ 1+λN. This is independent of the choice of N because rescaling N is a linear automorphism of G_a.
(9) Concretely, L ≅ V̌(𝒩), the covariant vector bundle (whose sections are sections of 𝒩) attached to the invertible subsheaf 𝒩 ⊂ Lie(G) = M spanned locally by the N. In other words, L is identified with the line of nilpotents in the Lie algebra of the Borel's unipotent radical, via the exponential N ↦ 1+N.

On the next page this is used to say that choosing a generator e amounts to trivialising this line bundle. It then feeds into the analysis of the 'loop equation' (132), where a factor ε_1(μ−1) is viewed as a section of such an additive subgroup L_1.

One can add that L is also canonically the vector bundle of translations of the affine line bundle E = P \ {x_∞}. This is isomorphic to the conormal line of P at x_∞, and the next page's margin alludes to the translation identification.
errors: No substantive error. The notation e^λ for 1+λN with λ a unit is an abuse, but harmless: for N^2 = 0 it equals exp(λN) and extends to all λ ∈ G_a, which is what (8) does.
Sentence (6)–(7) is grammatically unfinished ('donnera un sous ... sous-groupe additif borélien'), but the mathematics is clear.

ideas.what: Unipotent radicals of Borels in a form of SL_2/GL_2 (from an Azumaya quaternion algebra) correspond to sections of the Brauer–Severi conic.
ideas.modern_name: Scheme of Borel subgroups of a reductive group scheme ≅ the associated Brauer–Severi variety
ideas.where_published: SGA 3, Exp. XXII (scheme of Borel subgroups); Brauer–Severi in Grothendieck, 'Le groupe de Brauer I'

ideas.what: A one-dimensional unipotent subgroup (Borel additive subgroup) carries a canonical line-bundle structure, isomorphic to V̌ of the line of nilpotents in the Lie algebra, via N ↦ 1+N.
ideas.modern_name: Vector group structure on the root subgroup / unipotent radical; exponential isomorphism U_α ≅ W(g_α)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Demazure–Grothendieck, SGA 3 (root subgroups as vector groups)

ideas.what: Regular unipotent / regular nilpotent sections in relative form, with the equivalence e ~ e^λ.
ideas.modern_name: Regular unipotent elements (Steinberg); Kostant principal nilpotents

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully redoes, in the relative setting of a quaternion Azumaya algebra, the standard fact that the unipotent radical of a Borel is canonically a line bundle (SGA 3's U_α ≅ W(g_α)). It is preparatory bookkeeping for the 'loop equation' and contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Bottom of page: the formula reads 'e: G_a ⥲ L, e(λ) = e^λ = 1+λN' (G_a, not 'Ga' garbled).
'le 1-groupe [?] en' is plausibly 'le sous-groupe à 1-paramètre' / 'le groupe à un paramètre' ('comme le 1-groupe des').
In (9), '𝒩 ⊂ 𝔤.M' likely denotes the invertible subsheaf of nilpotents inside the Lie algebra 𝔤 = M (i.e. Lie(G) = M).
